AchReturn.table_description: This table records ACH (Automated Clearing House) payment returns, capturing instances where ACH debits or credits initiated by the company were rejected and returned by the receiving or originating bank. It supports treasury operations by tracking return volumes, amounts, and reasons to monitor payment failure rates, identify problematic accounts or counterparties, and manage NACHA compliance and return rate thresholds. Business questions answered include return rate analysis by reason code, exposure from unauthorized transaction disputes, and operational health of the ACH payment channel.

columns.amount: The dollar amount of the original ACH transfer that was returned, expressed as a decimal value.
columns.returnCategory: A high-level business classification of the return reason, such as UNAUTHORIZED, INVALID_ACCT, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, or OTHER, used for operational reporting and trend analysis.
columns.returnDate: The date on which the ACH return was received and recorded, used for aging analysis and compliance tracking against NACHA return windows.
columns.returnReasonCode: The standardized NACHA return reason code (e.g., R01 for insufficient funds, R03 for no account, R10 for customer advises unauthorized) assigned by the receiving or returning bank.
columns.originalTransfer: A reference to the original ACH transfer record that was returned, linking this return to its source transaction for reconciliation and dispute management.
columns.originatedBy: A reference to the entity or system that originated the original ACH transfer, such as a vendor, counterparty, or internal payment process, used to attribute returns to their source.

AchTransaction.table_description: The AchTransaction class mapped to lpp.transfer represents Automated Clearing House (ACH) electronic fund transfers processed through the banking network, capturing debit and credit movements between bank accounts for payroll, vendor payments, and consumer transactions. This table supports treasury operations by enabling reconciliation of ACH settlements, monitoring payment float, and tracking high-volume batch payment activity. Business questions answered include ACH transaction volumes by counterparty, settlement timing analysis, and identifying failed or returned ACH entries.

Acquirer.table_description: Stores the reference data for card payment acquirers (merchant acquiring banks and payment processors) that process card transactions on behalf of the retail company across its operating regions. Each acquirer record represents a contractual acquiring relationship used to route, settle, and reconcile card-present and card-not-present payments. This table supports treasury questions around acquirer concentration risk, settlement account mapping, regional acquiring strategy, and affiliated banking relationships.

columns.code: A short, system-readable unique identifier for the acquirer used as a foreign key in transaction, settlement, and fee records (e.g., ADYEN, FISERV).
columns.name: The full legal or trading name of the acquiring entity, including parent company context where relevant (e.g., Elavon (US Bancorp), Fiserv (First Data)).
columns.region: The geographic operating region in which this acquirer processes transactions for the company, aligned to standard treasury region codes such as AMER or EMEA.
columns.affiliatedBank: Reference to an affiliated or parent banking institution associated with this acquirer, used to map acquiring relationships to broader bank counterparty exposure and concentration analysis.
columns.settlementAccount: Reference to the specific bank or treasury account into which this acquirer remits settled card proceeds, used to reconcile daily settlement flows and cash positioning.

AcquirerContract.table_description: Stores the contractual terms negotiated between the retailer and its card acquirers, defining the commercial and operational conditions under which card payment processing services are provided. Each record represents a distinct acquirer contract period, capturing pricing, settlement timing, service-level commitments, and contract validity windows. This table supports treasury and payments questions around acquiring cost analysis, SLA compliance monitoring, contract renewal planning, and settlement liquidity forecasting.

columns.effectiveFrom: The date on which this acquirer contract becomes legally active and its terms begin to apply to card transaction processing.
columns.effectiveTo: The date on which this acquirer contract expires or is scheduled to terminate, marking the end of the contractual terms.
columns.processorMarginBps: The acquirer's processing fee expressed in basis points, representing the margin charged on each card transaction settled under this contract.
columns.settlementLagDays: The number of business days between the transaction authorization date and the date funds are settled into the retailer's bank account by the acquirer.
columns.status: The current lifecycle status of the contract, indicating whether the agreement is active, expired, or otherwise inactive.
columns.uptimeSlaPct: The minimum system availability percentage guaranteed by the acquirer in the service-level agreement, representing the contractual uptime commitment for payment processing infrastructure.
columns.withAcquirer: A reference to the acquirer entity (financial institution or payment processor) that is the counterparty to this contract.

AcquirerSlaMetric.table_description: The acquirer_sla_metric table stores daily service-level agreement (SLA) performance metrics for each card acquirer, capturing operational reliability and processing quality over time. It enables treasury and payments teams to monitor acquirer performance against contractual obligations, identify underperforming acquirers, and support renegotiation or switching decisions. Business questions answered include: Which acquirers are consistently failing authorization rate or uptime thresholds? Are settlement obligations being met on time across all acquiring relationships?

columns.authRatePct: The percentage of card authorization attempts that were successfully approved by the acquirer on the measurement date, expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 98.189 means 98.189%).
columns.measurementDate: The calendar date for which the SLA metrics were recorded, used to track acquirer performance trends over time.
columns.settlementOnTimePct: The percentage of transactions settled by the acquirer within the contractually agreed settlement window on the measurement date, indicating timeliness of fund transfer to the merchant.
columns.uptimePct: The percentage of time the acquirer's payment processing infrastructure was available and operational during the measurement date, reflecting system reliability against uptime SLA commitments.
columns.forAcquirer: A reference to the acquirer entity (linked via RDF relationship) for which these SLA metrics are recorded, identifying which acquiring bank or payment processor the row pertains to.

ApInvoice.table_description: The ap_invoice table stores accounts payable invoice records within the treasury and payments system, capturing the timing and aging of outstanding or processed vendor invoices. It supports cash flow forecasting, working capital analysis, and payment obligation tracking by categorizing invoices into rolling time windows. This table answers business questions such as how many invoices are due or were processed within recent periods and how payable balances trend over short, medium, and long-term horizons.

columns.inLast30Days: Boolean or numeric flag indicating whether the invoice falls within the most recent 30-day window, used for short-term cash outflow analysis and near-term payment obligation reporting.
columns.inLast90Days: Boolean or numeric flag indicating whether the invoice falls within the most recent 90-day window, used for quarterly working capital assessments and medium-term payables trend analysis.
columns.inLastYear: Boolean or numeric flag indicating whether the invoice falls within the most recent 12-month window, used for annual spend analysis, vendor payment history reporting, and year-over-year payables benchmarking.

ArInvoice.table_description: The ArInvoice table stores accounts receivable invoice records for the retail organization, capturing outstanding and settled customer or counterparty invoices relevant to cash flow forecasting and liquidity management. It supports treasury questions around receivables aging, expected cash inflows, and working capital optimization. The table enables analysis of invoice activity across rolling time windows to assess collection velocity and DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) trends.

columns.inLast30Days: Boolean or numeric flag indicating whether the invoice was created, due, or settled within the last 30 calendar days, used for short-term cash inflow forecasting.
columns.inLast90Days: Boolean or numeric flag indicating whether the invoice falls within the last 90 calendar days, supporting quarterly receivables aging and working capital reporting.
columns.inLastYear: Boolean or numeric flag indicating whether the invoice activity occurred within the last 12 months, used for annual trend analysis of accounts receivable and revenue recognition.

Balance.table_description: The lpp.bank_statement_balance table stores point-in-time balance snapshots for bank accounts, capturing opening, closing, and available balances alongside rolling inflow aggregates over multiple lookback windows. It supports treasury cash positioning, liquidity monitoring, and cash flow trend analysis across the retail organization. Business users can query this table to understand current and historical cash positions, identify liquidity trends, and reconcile bank statement balances against internal records.

columns.availableBalance: The funds immediately available for use in the account at the time of the snapshot, net of holds, pending transactions, or reserve requirements.
columns.closingBalance: The ending ledger balance of the bank account at the close of the statement period or snapshot date.
columns.inLast30Days: The total amount of funds received into the account over the trailing 30-day period from the snapshot date, used for short-term cash flow analysis.
columns.inLast7Days: The total amount of funds received into the account over the trailing 7-day period from the snapshot date, used for near-term liquidity monitoring.
columns.inLast90Days: The total amount of funds received into the account over the trailing 90-day period from the snapshot date, supporting medium-term cash flow trend analysis.
columns.inLastYear: The total amount of funds received into the account over the trailing 12-month period from the snapshot date, used for annual cash flow benchmarking and planning.
columns.isLatestSnapshot: A boolean flag indicating whether this record represents the most recent balance snapshot for the associated bank account, used to filter for current cash positions.
columns.openingBalance: The starting ledger balance of the bank account at the beginning of the statement period or snapshot date, used as the baseline for reconciliation and period-over-period analysis.

BalanceSnapshot.table_description: The cash_balance table stores point-in-time snapshots of cash balances held across bank accounts, capturing the monetary position in a specific currency as of a given business date. It supports treasury liquidity monitoring, daily cash positioning, and multi-currency cash reporting for the organization. Business questions it answers include: What is the end-of-day cash balance for a given account on a specific date? What is the total cash position across all accounts in a given currency?

columns.amount: The monetary balance amount recorded for the account as of the snapshot date, expressed in the account's designated currency, which may be positive (credit balance), zero, or negative (overdraft position).
columns.asOfDate: The business date for which the balance snapshot is recorded, representing the point-in-time as of which the cash position is measured (e.g., end of business day).
columns.currencyCode: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code indicating the currency in which the balance amount is denominated (e.g., AUD, BRL, EUR).
columns.status: The processing or confirmation status of the balance snapshot, indicating whether the balance record has been confirmed, is pending reconciliation, or carries another workflow state.
columns.forAccount: A reference to the bank account entity to which this balance snapshot belongs, linking the balance record to a specific account in the treasury system.

Bank.table_description: Stores reference data for banking institutions that the company maintains relationships with, including counterparty banks, acquiring banks, FX dealing banks, and custodians. Each record represents a unique legal banking entity identified by global standards such as BIC and LEI. This table supports counterparty risk analysis, bank relationship management, and regulatory reporting by linking transactional data to formally identified financial institutions.

columns.bic: The Bank Identifier Code (SWIFT BIC) uniquely identifying the bank for international payment routing and messaging.
columns.code: An internal short code used by the treasury system to reference the bank across transactions, accounts, and reports.
columns.lei: The Legal Entity Identifier (LEI), a globally recognized 20-character alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the bank as a legal entity for regulatory and counterparty risk purposes.
columns.name: The full legal name of the banking institution as registered with regulatory authorities.
columns.brain:boardMemberOverlap: Indicates whether this bank shares one or more board members with the company or other related entities, used for conflict-of-interest and governance risk assessments.
columns.brain:sharedParentInstitution: Identifies whether this bank shares a common parent institution with another bank in the system, supporting counterparty concentration risk analysis and group-level exposure aggregation.

BankAccount.table_description: Stores the master registry of bank accounts held by the retail organization across all financial institutions, branches, and currencies. Each record represents a distinct bank account used for treasury operations including cash concentration, disbursements, collections, FX settlements, and intercompany transfers. This table answers business questions such as: which accounts are held at which banks and branches, what currency is each account denominated in, and which legal entity or business unit owns each account.

columns.code: A unique alphanumeric identifier or account code assigned internally to reference this bank account within the treasury management system.
columns.atBranch: A reference to the specific bank branch (RDF resource) where this account is physically or administratively held, linking to branch-level details such as location and sort code.
columns.hasCurrency: A reference to the currency (RDF resource) in which this bank account is denominated, such as USD, EUR, or GBP, governing the currency of all transactions and balances.
columns.heldAt: A reference to the financial institution (RDF resource) at which this account is maintained, identifying the bank or counterparty holding the funds.
columns.ownedBy: A reference to the legal entity, business unit, or organizational division (RDF resource) that owns and is responsible for this bank account within the corporate structure.

BankAccountSignatory.table_description: The BankAccountSignatory table records the authorized individuals who have signing or releasing authority over specific bank accounts, defining their roles, spending limits, and recertification schedules. It supports treasury governance and controls by answering questions such as who is authorized to sign or release payments on a given account, up to what monetary threshold, and when their authorization must be reviewed and reconfirmed. This table is critical for segregation-of-duties enforcement, audit compliance, and bank mandate management across the organization.

columns.authorityLimitAmount: The maximum monetary amount in the account currency up to which this signatory is authorized to approve or release transactions on the linked bank account.
columns.nextRecertifyDueDate: The date by which this signatory's authorization must be formally reviewed and recertified to remain active and compliant with internal treasury governance policies.
columns.role: The functional role assigned to this signatory on the bank account, such as SIGNER_A or SIGNER_B for dual-control signing tiers, or RELEASER for payment release authority.
columns.status: The current authorization status of the signatory record, indicating whether the signatory is actively permitted to act on the account (e.g., ACTIVE) or has been suspended or revoked.
columns.onBankAccount: A reference to the bank account entity for which this signatory authorization applies, linking the signatory to a specific account in the treasury system.
columns.signatoryUser: A reference to the user or person entity who holds this signatory authorization, identifying the individual granted the specified role and authority limit on the bank account.

BankBranch.table_description: Stores individual bank branch locations for financial institutions used in the company's treasury and banking relationships, identifying specific branches by their institution and geographic location. This table enables treasury operations to route payments, manage cash pooling structures, and assign transactions to the correct physical or operational branch of a banking partner. It supports regulatory reporting, counterparty risk management, and FX hedging by pinpointing which branch of a bank holds accounts or executes transactions.

columns.code: A unique alphanumeric identifier for a bank branch, formatted as BR_{BankAcronym}_{LocationCode}, used to reference specific branches in transaction, account, and hedging records.
columns.countryCode: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code indicating the country where the bank branch is physically located or operationally domiciled, used for jurisdictional and regulatory classification.
columns.branchOf: A reference linking this branch to its parent banking institution (BankInstitution entity), establishing the ownership hierarchy between a branch and its owning bank.

BankFee.table_description: The BankFee table records individual fees charged by banking partners to the company's accounts, capturing the fee amount, currency, and service type for a given reporting date. It supports treasury operations by enabling analysis of bank service costs, contract compliance verification against negotiated rate cards, and fee optimization across banking relationships. Business questions answered include which banks are charging above contracted rates, total fee spend by service type or account, and period-over-period fee trends.

columns.asOfDate: The reporting date on which the bank fee was recorded or assessed, used for period-based fee analysis and trending.
columns.currencyCode: The ISO 4217 currency code in which the fee amount is denominated, such as USD, enabling multi-currency fee aggregation and conversion.
columns.exceedsRateCard: A boolean flag indicating whether the charged fee exceeds the negotiated rate card agreement with the bank, used to identify billing discrepancies and contract violations.
columns.feeAmount: The monetary value of the individual bank fee charged, expressed in the associated currency, used to calculate total bank service costs.
columns.chargedBy: A reference to the banking institution or counterparty that levied the fee, linking to the bank or financial institution entity in the ontology.
columns.feeServiceType: A categorical reference describing the type of banking service for which the fee was charged, such as wire transfer, account maintenance, or lockbox processing.
columns.forAccount: A reference to the specific bank account against which the fee was assessed, linking this fee record to the corresponding BankAccount entity.
columns.governedBy: A reference to the contractual agreement or rate card that defines the terms and expected pricing for this fee, used to validate charges against negotiated terms.

Bond.table_description: This table stores information about credit facilities and bond-like financing arrangements available to the organization, capturing the terms, limits, and status of borrowing facilities extended by financial institutions. It supports treasury questions related to available liquidity, debt capacity, and financing structure. Business users can leverage this table to assess credit availability, monitor facility utilization, and manage capital structure decisions.

Branch.table_description: The lpp.bank_branch table stores geographic hierarchy information for bank branches, linking each branch to its containing country and region. This table supports treasury operations by enabling analysts to group and filter bank branches by geographic location for cash position reporting, liquidity management, and regulatory compliance across different jurisdictions. It answers questions such as which branches operate within a specific country or region, supporting multi-entity treasury structures common in large retail organizations.

columns.inCountry: Stores the country in which the bank branch is located, used to group branches by national jurisdiction for regulatory reporting and cross-border cash management.
columns.inRegion: Stores the regional classification of the bank branch (e.g., geographic region or sub-national territory), enabling aggregation of cash positions and transaction activity at the regional level.

CapitalAllocationActual.table_description: Stores actual capital allocation amounts by bucket for a given reporting period, tracking how the company has deployed its available capital across strategic priorities such as capital expenditures, mergers and acquisitions, dividends, debt reduction, and share buybacks. Each record captures the realized dollar amount allocated to a specific bucket alongside the framework target percentage, enabling treasury and finance teams to compare actual capital deployment against predefined strategic allocation targets. This table supports questions about capital discipline, shareholder return execution, and variance analysis between planned and actual capital allocation.

columns.amount: The actual monetary amount in dollars allocated to the corresponding capital bucket during the reporting period.
columns.bucket: The capital allocation category representing the strategic use of funds, such as CAPEX (capital expenditures), M_AND_A (mergers and acquisitions), DIVIDENDS, DEBT_PAYDOWN, or BUYBACKS (share repurchases).
columns.frameworkTargetPct: The target percentage of total available capital that the company's capital allocation framework prescribes should be deployed to this bucket, used as a benchmark against actual allocations.
columns.periodDate: The end date of the reporting period for which the capital allocation actuals are recorded, typically representing a quarter-end or fiscal period close date.
columns.forCompany: A reference to the company entity for which this capital allocation record applies, supporting multi-entity or peer comparison scenarios within the data warehouse.

CardAuthorization.table_description: Stores individual card authorization events captured at the point of authorization request and response, representing the real-time approval or decline of card-based payment transactions across the company's acquiring network. Each record corresponds to a single authorization attempt, enabling treasury and payments teams to monitor approval rates, decline patterns, 3DS authentication behavior, and authorization response latency. This table supports operational KPIs such as authorization success rates, fraud exposure by transaction size band, and acquirer or network performance benchmarking.

columns.amount: The monetary value of the transaction submitted for authorization, expressed as a decimal in the currency indicated by currencyCode.
columns.auth3dsStatus: Indicates the outcome or applicability of 3D Secure authentication for this authorization attempt, such as NOT_ATTEMPTED when 3DS was not invoked.
columns.authDecision: The final authorization decision returned by the issuer or authorization engine, such as APPROVED or DECLINED.
columns.authRequestTimestamp: The UTC timestamp at which the authorization request was initiated and sent for processing, used to measure authorization latency and volume patterns over time.
columns.authResponseTimestamp: The UTC timestamp at which the authorization response was received, used in conjunction with authRequestTimestamp to calculate end-to-end response time.
columns.cnpIndicator: Boolean flag indicating whether the transaction was Card Not Present (CNP), distinguishing between in-person and remote or online payment scenarios.
columns.currencyCode: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the transaction amount is denominated, such as USD.
columns.declineReasonCode: The issuer or network-provided reason code explaining why an authorization was declined; null or absent when the transaction was approved.
columns.responseTimeMs: The elapsed time in milliseconds between the authorization request and response, used to assess authorization network and acquirer performance.
columns.transactionSizeBand: A categorical band grouping the transaction amount into defined ranges such as LT_25, 25_100, 100_500, or 500_5000, used for segmentation and reporting of authorization activity by value tier.
columns.authForPos: Indicates whether the authorization was initiated for a point-of-sale terminal context; no samples available in current dataset.
columns.onNetwork: Indicates the payment network over which the authorization was routed, such as Visa or Mastercard; no samples available in current dataset.
columns.viaAcquirer: Identifies the acquiring institution or processor through which the authorization request was submitted; no samples available in current dataset.

CardNetwork.table_description: Stores the reference catalog of payment card networks accepted or processed by the company, including both major global networks and proprietary private-label programs. This table supports treasury and payments analysis by classifying transaction volumes, interchange costs, fraud rates, and acceptance fees by network type. It enables reporting on network concentration risk, cost-of-acceptance benchmarking, and FX exposure segmentation across credit, charge, debit, and private-label rails.

columns.code: A short uppercase identifier for the card network used as a foreign key in transaction and acquiring tables (e.g., VISA, MASTERCARD, COSTCO_PRIVATE).
columns.name: The full human-readable display name of the card network as used in business reports and dashboards (e.g., Visa, American Express, Costco Private Label).
columns.networkType: Classifies the card network by its payment rail and credit structure, with values such as CREDIT, CHARGE, PRIVATE_LABEL, and DEBIT_PIN, enabling cost and risk segmentation across different funding and liability models.

CardPaymentRollup.table_description: Stores daily rolled-up card payment settlement batches summarizing gross sales, fee components, and net settlement amounts processed through card acquiring channels. Each record represents an aggregated settlement batch for a specific date, enabling treasury to monitor daily card acceptance costs, calculate effective interchange rates, and reconcile net cash received from acquirers against point-of-sale gross sales. This table supports cost-of-acceptance analysis, acquirer fee auditing, and daily cash position forecasting for card-based revenue streams.

columns.asOfDate: The business date for which the card settlement batch was processed and aggregated, used as the primary time dimension for daily treasury reconciliation.
columns.batchCount: The number of individual settlement batches consolidated into this rollup record for the given date, indicating whether single or multiple batch submissions occurred.
columns.grossSalesAmount: The total face value of card sales transactions submitted for settlement before any fee deductions, representing gross card revenue for the day.
columns.interchangeAmount: The interchange fees assessed by the card networks and paid to issuing banks, representing typically the largest component of card acceptance cost deducted from gross sales.
columns.netSettlementAmount: The actual net amount funded by the acquirer to the company after all fees are deducted from gross sales, representing the cash received in the settlement bank account.
columns.networkAssessmentAmount: The fees charged by the card network (e.g., Visa, Mastercard) for transaction processing and network access, separate from interchange and assessed on gross volume.
columns.processorMarginAmount: The acquirer or payment processor's service margin fee deducted from gross sales, representing the processor's revenue for transaction handling and settlement services.
columns.onNetwork: Identifies the card network (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, Amex) over which the settlement batch was processed, used to segment acceptance costs and volumes by network.
columns.viaAcquirer: Identifies the acquiring bank or payment processor that handled the settlement batch, used to attribute fees and net settlement amounts to specific acquirer relationships.

CardRebateEarning.table_description: The CardRebateEarning table tracks rebate income earned on corporate card spending by category and quarter, enabling treasury to monitor rebate program performance and optimize card usage to maximize cashback returns. It supports business questions such as which spend categories generate the most rebate value, how rebate yields trend across periods, and whether actual rebates align with program entitlements. This table is central to corporate card program management and working capital optimization.

columns.eligibleSpend: The gross card spend amount (in the reporting currency) that qualifies for rebate calculation under the corporate card program during the period, expressed as a decimal value.
columns.periodDate: The quarter-end date representing the reporting period for which the eligible spend and rebate earned figures are calculated, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.
columns.rebateEarned: The actual monetary rebate amount earned from the card issuer or program provider based on the eligible spend for the period and applicable rebate rate tiers.
columns.spendCategory: The business classification of the card expenditure used to segment rebate earnings, such as LOGISTICS, INVENTORY, UTILITIES, TRAVEL, or OTHER.
columns.underProgram: The identifier or name of the corporate card rebate program under which the eligible spend and rebate earning are being tracked, linking the record to a specific card issuer agreement or program tier.

CardRebateProgram.table_description: Stores the master definitions of card rebate programs negotiated between the company and its issuing bank partners, covering virtual cards, commercial cards, and purchasing cards. Each record represents a distinct rebate agreement identified by a program code, capturing the rebate rate (in basis points) the company earns when card spend meets the contractually defined target threshold. This table supports treasury questions around optimizing card program selection, benchmarking rebate yields across issuers, and projecting rebate income based on anticipated spend volumes.

columns.code: A unique alphanumeric identifier for the rebate program, typically encoding the issuer and card type (e.g., REB_JPM_VCARD for JPMorgan virtual card), used as the primary reference key across the data warehouse.
columns.programType: Classifies the card rebate program into a standardized category such as VIRTUAL_CARD, COMMERCIAL_CARD, or PURCHASING_CARD, reflecting the underlying payment instrument and its intended use case in accounts payable or procurement workflows.
columns.rebateBpsAtTarget: The rebate rate expressed in basis points (hundredths of a percent) that the company earns on eligible card spend when the program's target spend threshold is achieved within the measurement period.
columns.issuerBank: The name or identifier of the financial institution that issues the card and is contractually obligated to pay the rebate, linking this program to the company's banking relationship records.

CardSettlementBatch.table_description: The card_settlement_batch table records the financial summary of each card payment settlement batch processed through the acquiring network, capturing gross sales, interchange, network assessment, processor margin, and net settlement amounts per batch cycle. It tracks the key timestamps in the settlement lifecycle—from batch close through processor settlement to bank deposit—enabling treasury to monitor daily cash conversion, SLA compliance, and the cost breakdown of card acceptance. This table answers business questions such as: what net funds were deposited to our bank accounts from card sales on a given day, are our acquirers meeting settlement SLAs, and what is the blended cost of card acceptance by acquirer or network?

columns.bankDepositTimestamp: The UTC timestamp at which the net settlement funds were credited to the company's bank account following processor settlement.
columns.batchCloseTimestamp: The UTC timestamp at which the card terminal or point-of-sale system closed the settlement batch, marking the end of the transaction capture window.
columns.grossSalesAmount: The total face value of all card sales captured in the batch before any deductions for interchange, network assessments, or processor fees, expressed in the settlement currency.
columns.interchangeAmount: The interchange fee amount deducted from gross sales and remitted to the card-issuing banks as mandated by the card network, expressed in the settlement currency.
columns.netSettlementAmount: The actual amount deposited to the company's bank account after subtracting interchange, network assessment, and processor margin from gross sales, representing the true cash received.
columns.networkAssessmentAmount: The fee assessed by the card network (e.g., Visa, Mastercard) on the batch volume, deducted from gross sales as part of the cost of network participation.
columns.processorMarginAmount: The fee retained by the payment processor or acquirer for processing and settling the batch, representing the processor's revenue on the transaction volume.
columns.processorSettleTimestamp: The UTC timestamp at which the payment processor completed its internal settlement calculation and initiated the funds transfer to the company's bank account.
columns.slaMet: A boolean flag indicating whether the processor delivered settlement within the contractually agreed service level agreement timeframe for this batch.
columns.onNetwork: A reference to the card network (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, Amex) over which the transactions in this batch were processed and settled.
columns.settledTo: A reference to the bank account or financial institution destination to which the net settlement amount for this batch was deposited.
columns.viaAcquirer: A reference to the acquiring bank or payment processor that processed and settled this card settlement batch on behalf of the company.

CardSettlementLine.table_description: CardSettlementLine represents an individual line item within a card payment settlement batch, capturing the financial and geographic details of a single card transaction being settled. Each record links a settled transaction to its authorization and batch, enabling treasury teams to reconcile gross card receipts, calculate net interchange costs, and analyze cross-border transaction exposure by issuer geography. This table supports questions about interchange fee burdens, foreign-issued card volumes, and settlement-to-authorization matching.

columns.crossBorder: Indicates whether the card transaction was cross-border, meaning the issuer country differs from the merchant's country, which affects interchange rates and FX exposure.
columns.grossAmount: The gross transaction amount settled in the transaction currency before deducting interchange fees or other adjustments, representing the top-line card revenue for this line item.
columns.interchangeBps: The interchange fee rate applied to this settlement line expressed in basis points, used to calculate the cost of card acceptance charged by the card network to the acquirer.
columns.issuerCountry: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the bank or financial institution that issued the payment card, used to identify cross-border transactions and assess geographic risk concentration.
columns.inBatch: A reference to the parent card settlement batch that this line item belongs to, linking the individual settlement line to its aggregated batch for reconciliation purposes.
columns.settlesAuth: A reference to the original card authorization record that this settlement line is settling, enabling matching of settled transactions back to their corresponding authorization events.

CashFlow.table_description: The lpp.cash_flow table stores aggregated inbound cash flow metrics for treasury liquidity monitoring, capturing the total cash received into accounts over rolling time windows. It supports short-term and medium-term liquidity analysis, enabling treasury teams to assess cash inflow trends, forecast funding needs, and evaluate whether incoming cash adequately supports operational and capital requirements. This table is typically used in conjunction with outflow and balance data to produce net cash position and liquidity coverage reports.

columns.inLast30Days: The total amount of cash received into accounts during the most recent 30-day rolling period, used for monthly liquidity and cash inflow trend analysis.
columns.inLast7Days: The total amount of cash received into accounts during the most recent 7-day rolling period, used for short-term weekly cash inflow monitoring and near-term liquidity forecasting.
columns.inLast90Days: The total amount of cash received into accounts during the most recent 90-day rolling period, used for quarterly cash inflow analysis and medium-term treasury planning.
columns.inLastYear: The total amount of cash received into accounts during the most recent 365-day rolling period, used for annual cash inflow benchmarking, trend analysis, and long-term liquidity strategy.

CashForecast.table_description: The lpp.forecast_snapshot table stores point-in-time cash flow forecast snapshots used by treasury to project future liquidity positions across short-term and medium-term horizons. Each record represents a versioned forecast run identified by a reference date and a structured code, supporting both direct (cash-movement-based) and indirect (income-statement-based) forecasting methodologies. This table answers questions such as: what was the forecasted cash position as of a given date, how do forecast vintages compare over time, and which forecasting methodology was used for a given planning horizon.

columns.asOfDate: The reference date on which the forecast snapshot was generated or to which it applies, used to version forecasts and track how projections evolve over time.
columns.code: A structured alphanumeric identifier for the forecast snapshot encoding the as-of date and forecast frequency (e.g., FC_20230801_M), used as a unique key to retrieve or compare specific forecast runs.
columns.name: A human-readable label describing the forecast type and horizon, distinguishing between methodologies such as the 13-week direct forecast and the 18-month indirect forecast.

CashRollup.table_description: This table stores daily aggregated cash balances rolled up across multiple bank accounts for a specific legal entity and currency, derived from bank statement data. It provides a consolidated snapshot of total available cash on any given date, enabling treasury teams to monitor liquidity positions, track cash movements over time, and answer questions such as 'What was our total EUR cash balance across all accounts on a given date?' and 'How many accounts contributed to our cash position for a specific entity?'

columns.asOfDate: The calendar date for which the aggregated cash balance snapshot is recorded, representing the statement balance date as reported by the bank.
columns.currencyCode: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code (e.g., EUR) indicating the currency in which all aggregated balances in this row are denominated.
columns.nAccounts: The count of distinct bank accounts included in the cash rollup for this entity, currency, and date combination.
columns.totalCash: The sum of closing cash balances across all included bank accounts for the specified entity, currency, and date, expressed as a decimal numeric value in the stated currency.
columns.forEntity: A reference to the legal entity (e.g., a subsidiary or operating company) for which the cash rollup is aggregated, linking this record to the relevant organizational unit in the treasury structure.

Chargeback.table_description: The lpp.chargeback table records all payment disputes initiated against the company's merchant accounts, capturing the full lifecycle from initiation through resolution. It enables treasury and payments teams to monitor dispute volumes, track win/loss ratios, classify fraud versus merchant error, and analyze chargeback exposure by reason code and network. This table is central to fraud management reporting, acquiring cost control, and compliance with card network dispute rules.

columns.amount: The monetary value of the disputed transaction subject to the chargeback, expressed as a decimal in the account's base currency.
columns.classification: The categorization of the chargeback's root cause, distinguishing between TRUE_FRAUD (unauthorized use), FRIENDLY_FRAUD (illegitimate cardholder dispute), and MERCHANT_ERROR (fulfillment or processing mistake).
columns.initiatedDate: The calendar date on which the chargeback dispute was formally opened by the issuing bank or cardholder.
columns.reasonCategory: A high-level grouping of the dispute reason, such as FRAUD, DUPLICATE, NOT_AS_DESCRIBED, or NON_RECEIPT, used for trend analysis and reporting.
columns.reasonCode: The card network-specific reason code (e.g., Visa/Mastercard numeric codes) that precisely identifies the regulatory or procedural basis for the dispute.
columns.resolvedDate: The calendar date on which the chargeback case was closed, either through a final ruling, representment acceptance, or withdrawal.
columns.status: The current processing state of the chargeback, indicating whether it is INITIATED, REPRESENTED (contested by the merchant), WON (resolved in the merchant's favor), or LOST (resolved in the cardholder's favor).
columns.disputesAuth: A reference or flag linking the chargeback to the original authorization record associated with the disputed transaction.
columns.onNetwork: An indicator or identifier specifying which card network (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, Amex) is governing and processing the chargeback dispute.
columns.viaAcquirer: A reference to the acquiring bank or payment processor through which the chargeback was routed and managed on behalf of the merchant.

CheckPayment.table_description: The CheckPayment class mapped to the lpp.transfer table represents check-based payment transactions processed by the treasury and payments system. This table captures the lifecycle and details of check disbursements and receipts, supporting business questions around outstanding checks, cleared payments, vendor disbursements, and cash flow reconciliation. It serves as a key audit trail for paper-based payment instruments within the broader payments infrastructure.

CommercialPaperProgram.table_description: This table stores details about Commercial Paper Programs, which are short-term unsecured debt instruments used by the treasury to manage liquidity and fund operational needs. It captures program-level attributes such as authorized issuance limits, tenors, credit ratings, and dealer arrangements that support capital markets funding strategies. Business questions answered include: What is the total authorized commercial paper capacity? Which programs are active and what are their current outstanding balances relative to program limits?

Company.table_description: Stores master reference data for companies that interact with the treasury and payments ecosystem, including banks, payment processors, FX counterparties, card acquirers, and vendors. Each record represents a distinct legal or commercial entity identified by standard codes and legal entity identifiers. This table supports counterparty management, FX hedging relationship tracking, vendor negotiations, and peer benchmarking analyses.

columns.code: Internal alphanumeric identifier assigned to the company for use across treasury and payments systems.
columns.countryCode: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code representing the primary country of domicile or registration for the company.
columns.lei: Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) as defined by the Global LEI System (GLEIF), used for regulatory reporting, FX counterparty verification, and cross-border payment compliance.
columns.name: Full legal or commonly used business name of the company as recognized in contracts, banking agreements, and treasury records.
columns.brain:negotiatingHistory: AI-enriched attribute capturing the historical context and outcomes of commercial negotiations with this company, used to inform procurement strategy and counterparty relationship management.
columns.brain:strategicVendorTier: AI-enriched classification indicating the strategic importance tier of this company as a vendor or counterparty, used to prioritize treasury resources, credit exposure limits, and relationship investment.

CompanyFinancialMetric.table_description: This table stores quarterly and annual financial performance metrics for peer companies used in benchmarking and capital allocation analysis within the treasury function. It captures profitability, leverage, cash generation, and valuation metrics that enable treasury to compare the company's financial health against industry peers. Business questions answered include: how does our leverage compare to peers, what is the peer median WACC for discount rate benchmarking, and how do free cash flow yields stack up across the competitive set?

columns.debtToEbitda: The ratio of net debt to EBITDA for the reporting period, used as a leverage benchmark to assess how many years of operating earnings would be required to repay debt obligations.
columns.dilutedEps: Diluted earnings per share for the period, calculated using the fully diluted share count including options and convertible instruments, used as a profitability and valuation benchmark.
columns.dilutedSharesOutstanding: The total number of diluted shares outstanding for the company in the reporting period, including the effect of all potentially dilutive securities such as options and warrants.
columns.ebitda: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization for the reporting period, expressed in the company's reporting currency, used as a core measure of operating profitability in peer benchmarking.
columns.freeCashFlow: Operating cash flow less capital expenditures for the reporting period, representing the cash available to service debt, pay dividends, or fund investments, used in peer cash generation comparisons.
columns.netDebt: Total financial debt minus cash and cash equivalents for the reporting period; negative values indicate a net cash position, used to assess balance sheet strength and leverage relative to peers.
columns.periodDate: The calendar end date of the financial reporting period (quarter-end or year-end) to which the metrics apply, enabling time-series and cross-period comparisons.
columns.periodType: A code indicating the frequency of the reporting period, such as 'Q' for quarterly or 'A' for annual, used to filter and align metrics across peers on a consistent basis.
columns.revenue: Total net revenue recognized by the company in the reporting period, expressed in the company's reporting currency, used as a scale metric in peer benchmarking and ratio calculations.
columns.waccPct: The weighted average cost of capital expressed as a decimal percentage for the reporting period, reflecting the blended required return on equity and debt, used to benchmark discount rates and assess capital efficiency across peers.
columns.forCompany: A foreign key reference linking the financial metric record to the specific peer or subject company entity in the ontology for which these metrics are reported.

ConcentrationAccount.table_description: The ConcentrationAccount class represents bank accounts used in cash concentration and pooling structures, where funds from subsidiary or regional accounts are swept into a central treasury account to optimize liquidity and reduce idle cash. This table stores the defining attributes of each concentration account, including its banking relationships, account identifiers, and structural role within the cash management hierarchy. It supports treasury questions around intercompany funding, zero-balance account (ZBA) structures, notional pooling arrangements, and centralized liquidity management.

Counterparty.table_description: Stores counterparty records representing third-party entities involved in treasury and payments operations, including retail partners, acquiring banks, and aggregated consumer groups. Each record identifies an external party that may be associated with transactions, FX exposures, card acquiring flows, or intercompany settlements. This table answers business questions such as which counterparties are generating transaction volumes, which retail partners are exposed to FX risk, and how to segment cash flows by external party.

columns.code: A unique alphanumeric identifier for the counterparty used as a reference key across treasury and payments systems, with special codes such as RETAIL_CONSUMER representing aggregated groups rather than individual entities.
columns.name: The full descriptive name of the counterparty, identifying either a specific named retail or financial partner (e.g., Macys Partner 1, Selfridges Partner 5) or a consolidated category such as Aggregated Retail Consumer for bulk consumer transaction groupings.

CounterpartyExposure.table_description: This table tracks the company's financial exposure to individual counterparties (such as banks, brokers, or trading partners) as of specific snapshot dates, capturing the monetary value at risk or outstanding with each party. It supports treasury risk management by enabling monitoring of concentration risk, counterparty credit limits, and compliance with internal or regulatory exposure thresholds. Business questions answered include: What is our total exposure to a given bank or counterparty on a specific date, and how has that exposure trended over time?

columns.amount: The monetary value of the company's financial exposure to the counterparty as of the snapshot date, expressed in the specified currency.
columns.asOfDate: The date on which the exposure snapshot was recorded, used for point-in-time risk reporting and trend analysis.
columns.currencyCode: The ISO 4217 currency code in which the exposure amount is denominated, indicating the currency of the outstanding position.
columns.counterparty: The name or identifier of the external financial institution, broker, or trading partner to which the company has the recorded exposure.

Country.table_description: This table stores the set of countries in which the company operates, identified by their ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes. It serves as a reference dimension for treasury and payments analytics, enabling questions about geographic distribution of cash positions, FX exposure by country, card acquiring volumes, and regulatory jurisdiction for transactions. It underpins multi-currency hedging strategies and cross-border liquidity management across all operational regions.

columns.countryCode: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 two-letter country code uniquely identifying each country in which the company has treasury, payments, or banking operations.

CreditFacility.table_description: The lpp.credit_facility table records all corporate credit facilities available to the treasury, including revolving credit facilities, term loans, overdrafts, commercial paper programs, and intercompany lines. It captures the key economic and structural terms of each facility such as size, pricing, tenor, and counterparty, enabling treasury to monitor available liquidity headroom, upcoming maturities, borrowing costs, and lender exposure across currencies. This table supports questions about total committed credit capacity, weighted average cost of debt, facility utilization, and refinancing risk.

columns.code: A unique alphanumeric identifier for the credit facility, encoding key attributes such as facility type (RCF, TERM, OD, CP, IC), currency, and approximate size (e.g., CF_RCF_USD_2B is a USD 2 billion revolving credit facility).
columns.expirationDate: The date on which the facility commitment expires and the lender is no longer obligated to make funds available, which may differ from the maturity date for drawn balances.
columns.maturityDate: The final legal maturity date by which all outstanding drawn amounts under the facility must be fully repaid.
columns.principalAmount: The total committed or authorized principal amount of the facility in the facility's denomination currency, representing the maximum drawable capacity.
columns.rateBenchmark: The floating interest rate reference benchmark used to price the facility (e.g., SOFR for USD, ESTR for EUR, SONIA for GBP), to which the rate spread is added to determine the all-in borrowing cost.
columns.rateSpread: The margin or spread in basis points added to the rate benchmark to calculate the total interest rate payable on drawn amounts under the facility.
columns.status: The current operational status of the facility, indicating whether it is active, expired, cancelled, or in another lifecycle state.
columns.tradeDate: The date on which the credit facility agreement was executed or signed between the company and the lender(s).
columns.hasCurrency: A relationship linking the credit facility to its designated currency entity, identifying the currency in which the facility is denominated and drawn.
columns.lender: A relationship identifying the financial institution or syndicate member(s) providing the credit commitment under the facility.
columns.tradedBy: A relationship identifying the internal treasury desk, trader, or responsible party who negotiated or manages the credit facility on behalf of the company.

CreditRating.table_description: Stores credit ratings assigned by major rating agencies to companies tracked in the treasury system, capturing both historical and current ratings with their associated outlooks. This table supports treasury and capital allocation decisions by providing an up-to-date view of counterparty or corporate creditworthiness, enabling analysis of credit risk exposure across banking relationships, investment counterparties, and peer benchmarks. It answers questions such as which companies hold investment-grade ratings, which ratings are currently active, and how ratings have changed over time across agencies.

columns.agency: The credit rating agency that issued the rating, such as Moody's, S&P, or Fitch, identifying the source of the credit assessment.
columns.asOfDate: The date on which the credit rating was assigned or became effective, enabling point-in-time and historical rating analysis.
columns.isCurrent: A boolean flag indicating whether this rating record represents the most current active rating from the given agency, distinguishing current ratings from superseded historical ones.
columns.outlook: The rating agency's forward-looking assessment of the likely direction of the credit rating, such as Stable or Positive, indicating expected near-term credit trajectory.
columns.ratingGrade: The specific alphanumeric credit rating grade assigned by the agency, such as Aa3, A+, or BBB+, representing the assessed creditworthiness level of the rated entity.
columns.forCompany: A reference to the company entity that this credit rating applies to, linking the rating record to the specific organization being evaluated.

CrossBorderPaymentLeg.table_description: Stores individual legs of cross-border payment transactions, capturing the routing, cost, and FX components of each international payment movement between originating and destination countries. Each record represents a distinct payment corridor with its associated FX spread and lifting fee costs, enabling treasury to analyze the total cost of cross-border fund movements, benchmark corridor efficiency, and optimize routing decisions. This table supports business questions around payment corridor cost analysis, FX spread monitoring, and lifting fee benchmarking across international payment lanes.

columns.corridor: Identifies the high-level payment corridor as a directional pair of regional or country codes (e.g., US-EU, US-APAC), used to group and analyze cross-border payment flows between major trade zones.
columns.destinationCountry: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code representing the receiving country where funds are delivered at the end of the payment leg.
columns.fxSpreadBps: The foreign exchange spread charged on the payment leg expressed in basis points, representing the cost markup above the interbank mid-rate applied during currency conversion for this corridor.
columns.liftingFees: The flat or variable fee charged to execute and lift the payment through correspondent banking or payment networks, expressed in the transaction currency, representing the direct transaction cost excluding FX spread.
columns.originationCountry: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code representing the sending country where the payment leg originates, used to determine regulatory requirements, correspondent bank selection, and cost structure.

Currency.table_description: The Currency table is a reference master that enumerates every currency recognized within the treasury and payments system, identified by its ISO 4217 alphabetic code. It supports multi-currency operations across bank accounts, FX hedging positions, card acquiring settlements, and cross-border transactions. Business users rely on this table to resolve currency codes into human-readable names and to validate that all financial instruments and cash positions are denominated in supported currencies.

columns.code: The ISO 4217 three-letter alphabetic currency code that uniquely identifies each currency and serves as the primary key for joining to financial transactions, FX rates, and account balances throughout the data warehouse.
columns.name: The full, human-readable name of the currency corresponding to its ISO 4217 code, used for display purposes in reports, dashboards, and business-facing documentation.

Customer.table_description: This table stores third-party entity records representing external counterparties, customers, vendors, or financial institutions involved in treasury and payment transactions. It serves as a reference registry for identifying and classifying non-internal parties across bank relationships, FX counterparties, card acquiring partners, and fraud monitoring. Business questions it answers include who are the external entities transacting with the organization and how are they classified for compliance, credit risk, and payment routing purposes.

DebtMaturity.table_description: The lpp.borrowing table records the company's debt obligations and borrowing activity, capturing each loan or credit facility drawn down across currencies and legal entities. It supports treasury questions around debt maturity profiles, outstanding principal balances, all-in borrowing costs, and repayment status. This table is central to liquidity planning, debt scheduling, and interest expense analysis.

columns.allInCost: The total annualized cost of the borrowing expressed as a percentage, including interest rate, fees, and any applicable spreads.
columns.currencyCode: The ISO 4217 currency code in which the borrowing is denominated, indicating the currency of principal and repayment obligations.
columns.drawnAmount: The actual amount drawn down or utilized from the credit facility at the time of the transaction, which may differ from the total principal if partially drawn.
columns.maturityDate: The scheduled date on which the principal of the borrowing is due to be fully repaid or the facility expires.
columns.principalAmount: The original face value or notional principal amount of the borrowing at inception.
columns.status: The current lifecycle status of the borrowing, indicating whether it is active, outstanding, or has been fully repaid (e.g., REPAID).
columns.tradeDate: The date on which the borrowing was executed or the loan agreement was entered into.
columns.scheduledOn: The date on which a scheduled repayment or drawdown event is expected to occur, used for forward-looking debt service planning.
columns.tradedBy: The identifier of the treasury dealer, trader, or counterparty relationship manager responsible for executing or managing the borrowing.

DerivativeMtm.table_description: The DerivativeMtm table stores mark-to-market (MTM) valuations of derivative financial instruments held by the company for FX hedging or other risk management purposes, recorded as of specific valuation dates. Each row captures the fair value gain or loss of a derivative position in a given currency as of a reporting date, enabling treasury to monitor unrealized gains and losses on open derivative contracts. This table supports questions such as current hedge effectiveness, counterparty exposure by instrument, and period-over-period MTM movements across the derivatives portfolio.

columns.asOfDate: The valuation date as of which the mark-to-market amount is calculated, typically representing a weekly or period-end snapshot of the derivative's fair value.
columns.currencyCode: The ISO 4217 currency code in which the MTM amount is denominated, indicating the reporting or settlement currency of the derivative position.
columns.mtmAmount: The mark-to-market fair value of the derivative instrument as of the valuation date, expressed as a positive value for unrealized gains and a negative value for unrealized losses.
columns.counterparty: The name or identifier of the financial institution or trading counterparty on the other side of the derivative contract, used to assess counterparty credit risk and exposure concentration.
columns.valuesInstrument: The identifier or description of the specific derivative instrument being valued, such as an FX forward, swap, or option contract, linking the MTM record to the underlying hedging instrument.

Disbursement.table_description: The lpp.cash_flow table records disbursement transactions representing outgoing cash flows from the organization, including vendor payments, payroll, intercompany transfers, and other treasury-initiated disbursements. It serves as the foundational ledger for tracking cash outflows across bank accounts, enabling treasury teams to monitor liquidity positions, reconcile payments, and forecast short-term cash requirements. This table answers business questions around payment timing, disbursement volumes by category, and cash utilization across legal entities.

Entity.table_description: This table captures informal dependency relationships between entities within the treasury and payments knowledge graph, representing soft or undocumented linkages that exist outside formal contractual or hierarchical structures. It supports business questions around hidden exposure concentrations, counterparty risk adjacency, and operational interdependencies that may not surface through standard financial reporting. These relationships are critical for stress testing, contagion analysis, and understanding how disruptions to one entity may indirectly affect others across the treasury ecosystem.

columns.brain:informalDependency: Stores the target entity or relationship identifier representing an informal, non-contractual dependency between two entities, such as a shared service provider, common liquidity source, or operational reliance that has not been formally documented in agreements.

EquityAction.table_description: The EquityAction table records corporate equity events including share buybacks and dividend distributions executed by the company over time. Each record captures the financial details of a single equity action on a specific settlement date, enabling treasury teams to track capital return programs, monitor shareholder distributions, and analyze the cost and scale of buyback activity across quarters. This table supports questions around total capital returned to shareholders, dividend yield trends, buyback pricing efficiency, and shares retired over time.

columns.actionDate: The settlement or effective date on which the equity action (buyback or dividend) was executed or recorded.
columns.actionType: Classifies the type of equity action performed, either BUYBACK for share repurchase programs or DIVIDEND for cash distributions to shareholders.
columns.dividendPerShare: The declared cash dividend amount paid per share to shareholders, populated only when actionType is DIVIDEND.
columns.pricePerShare: The price per share at which shares were repurchased during a buyback, or the market reference price associated with the equity action.
columns.shares: The number of shares involved in the equity action, representing shares repurchased in a buyback or shares eligible for dividend payment.
columns.totalAmount: The total cash outlay in base currency for the equity action, representing aggregate buyback spend or total dividend distribution amount.
columns.forCompany: A reference to the company entity for which this equity action was performed, linking the record to the corresponding organization in the ontology.

Fact.table_description: This table stores linkage records that associate tribal knowledge entities — such as business rules, expert insights, calculations, or contextual notes — with specific data objects across the treasury and payments data warehouse. It enables the system to attach institutional knowledge directly to relevant entities like bank accounts, transactions, FX positions, or fraud cases, ensuring that domain expertise is discoverable and queryable alongside structured data. Business questions answered include: what expert knowledge or business rules apply to a given treasury entity, and which entities share common tribal knowledge annotations.

columns.brain:appliesTo_1: References the first target entity or data object to which a piece of tribal knowledge applies, such as a specific bank account, transaction, or FX hedge record.
columns.brain:appliesTo_2: References the second target entity or data object to which a piece of tribal knowledge applies, supporting many-to-one knowledge linkage across treasury domains.
columns.brain:appliesTo_3: References the third target entity or data object to which a piece of tribal knowledge applies, enabling broad annotation of related instruments or positions.
columns.brain:appliesTo_4: References the fourth target entity or data object to which a piece of tribal knowledge applies, extending linkage to card acquiring or fraud-related entities.
columns.brain:appliesTo_5: References the fifth target entity or data object to which a piece of tribal knowledge applies, covering capital allocation or cash position records.
columns.brain:appliesTo_6: References the sixth target entity or data object to which a piece of tribal knowledge applies, supporting peer benchmark or counterparty entity annotations.
columns.brain:appliesTo_7: References the seventh target entity or data object to which a piece of tribal knowledge applies, allowing flexible multi-entity knowledge association.
columns.brain:appliesTo_8: References the eighth target entity or data object to which a piece of tribal knowledge applies, completing the set of linkable treasury and payments entities for a given knowledge record.

FedNowTransaction.table_description: The FedNowTransaction table (lpp.transfer) captures real-time payment transactions processed through the FedNow instant payment rail, enabling the treasury team to monitor, reconcile, and report on immediate fund transfers between bank accounts. It supports business questions around intraday liquidity management, real-time cash positioning, and settlement confirmation for instant payments. This table serves as the authoritative record for FedNow-facilitated transfers, linking payment activity to broader cash flow and bank account management workflows.

FeeServiceType.table_description: This table is a reference catalog of standardized bank service fee types used to classify charges assessed by banking partners against corporate accounts. It provides a controlled vocabulary for categorizing fees related to account maintenance, transaction processing, wire transfers, ACH activity, and statement delivery. Treasury teams use this table to analyze bank fee structures, benchmark service costs across banking relationships, and support fee negotiation and allocation workflows.

columns.code: A short numeric identifier uniquely representing a specific bank service fee type, used as a foreign key in fee transaction and bank analysis tables.
columns.name: A human-readable label describing the bank service fee type, such as account maintenance charges, wire transfer fees (domestic or international), ACH credits, or statement delivery costs.

ForecastActual.table_description: This table stores period-end comparisons between forecasted and actual cash outflows across key treasury driver categories, enabling treasury teams to measure forecast accuracy and identify variance drivers. It supports cash forecasting governance, liquidity planning reviews, and variance attribution by category such as payroll, AP disbursements, taxes, and capital expenditures. It is used to answer questions such as which cash flow categories are most frequently over- or under-forecast, and how forecast accuracy trends over time by entity and currency.

columns.actualOutflow: The realized cash outflow amount for the given driver category and period, expressed in the specified currency.
columns.asOfDate: The month-end date representing the period for which the forecast-versus-actual comparison is being evaluated.
columns.currencyCode: The ISO 4217 currency code in which both the forecasted and actual outflow amounts are denominated.
columns.driverCategory: The treasury classification of the cash flow driver being compared, such as AP_DISBURSEMENT, PAYROLL, TAX, AR_COLLECTION, FX_REVAL, or CAPEX.
columns.forecastedOutflow: The projected cash outflow amount that was estimated for the given driver category and period prior to the close date.
columns.varianceAmount: The absolute difference between actual and forecasted outflow amounts, where a positive value indicates actual exceeded forecast and a negative value indicates actual was below forecast.
columns.variancePct: The percentage difference between actual and forecasted outflow, expressing forecast error as a rounded percentage of the forecasted amount.
columns.forEntity: A reference to the legal entity or business unit for which this forecast-versus-actual comparison applies.

ForecastLine.table_description: The lpp.forecast_cash_flow table stores projected cash inflow and outflow amounts for each line of a treasury cash flow forecast, organized by entity, currency, and driver category as of a specific forecast date. It supports liquidity planning and funding decisions by allowing treasury teams to model expected cash movements across business units and currencies. This table answers questions such as 'What are the forecasted net cash positions by entity and currency for the upcoming period?' and 'How do projected inflows compare to outflows for a given forecast scenario?'

columns.asOfDate: The reference date for which the forecast cash flow projections are calculated, representing the snapshot point in time for the forecast.
columns.currencyCode: The ISO currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP) denoting the denomination in which the forecasted inflows and outflows are expressed.
columns.driverCategory: A classification label identifying the business driver or category behind the forecasted cash movement, such as merchandise payables, membership fees, or capital expenditures.
columns.forecastedInflow: The projected amount of cash expected to be received by the entity during the forecast period, expressed in the specified currency.
columns.forecastedOutflow: The projected amount of cash expected to be disbursed by the entity during the forecast period, expressed in the specified currency.
columns.forEntity: A reference to the legal entity or business unit for which this forecast cash flow line is being projected.
columns.forForecast: A reference to the parent forecast scenario or forecast run to which this individual cash flow line belongs, linking it to a specific forecast version or cycle.

FraudLoss.table_description: The FraudLoss table records confirmed fraud loss events across all payment channels and transaction types, capturing the financial impact, fraud mechanism, and authentication context of each incident. It supports treasury and payments risk questions such as: What is our total fraud loss exposure by channel or authentication method? How do true fraud losses compare to friendly fraud over time? Which fraud vectors are driving the highest losses? Each record represents a discrete fraud loss realization, optionally linked to the detection event that triggered it.

columns.authMethod: The authentication method in use at the time of the fraudulent transaction, indicating whether 3D Secure challenge, frictionless 3DS, no 3DS, or no authentication was applied.
columns.channel: The commerce channel through which the fraudulent transaction occurred, such as in-warehouse point-of-sale, e-commerce, or membership renewal.
columns.fraudVector: The attack method or fraud typology used to perpetrate the loss, such as social engineering or card-not-present fraud.
columns.lossAmount: The confirmed monetary value of the fraud loss in the local or reporting currency, representing the net financial impact recognized for this fraud event.
columns.lossCategory: The classification of the fraud loss as either true fraud (unauthorized third-party fraud) or friendly fraud (disputed legitimate transactions, typically chargeback abuse).
columns.lossDate: The calendar date on which the fraud loss was recognized or finalized, used for period-over-period loss trending and reserve calculations.
columns.fromDetectionEvent: A reference linking this fraud loss record to the upstream fraud detection event that identified or flagged the transaction, enabling traceability from detection through to confirmed loss realization.

FraudLossEvent.table_description: The lpp.fraud_detection_event table records individual fraud detection outcomes for payment transactions, capturing the system's classification and disposition of each event as it passes through fraud screening. Each record represents a single fraud evaluation result tied to a specific transaction, enabling treasury and payments teams to monitor fraud exposure, block rates, and review queue volumes. This table supports business questions around fraud loss quantification, transaction approval rates, and the effectiveness of fraud controls across payment channels.

columns.fraudCategoryLabel: The fraud risk classification label assigned by the fraud detection engine, indicating the outcome category of the evaluation such as ALLOW for approved transactions, REVIEW for transactions flagged for manual inspection, or BLOCK for transactions rejected due to suspected fraud.
columns.status: The current processing status of the fraud detection event, reflecting the actionable disposition of the transaction as ALLOW (permitted to proceed), REVIEW (held for further investigation), or BLOCK (declined due to fraud risk).
columns.relatedToTransaction: A reference linking this fraud detection event to the associated payment transaction record, enabling join traversal between fraud outcomes and the underlying transaction details such as amount, merchant, and account.

FxExposure.table_description: The fx_exposure_forecast table stores the company's projected foreign currency exposure positions as of specific reporting dates, capturing both long and short exposures across different tenors and currencies. It supports treasury hedging decisions by quantifying the gross currency risk the company faces over upcoming time horizons before hedging instruments are applied. Business questions answered include: what is our unhedged FX exposure by currency and tenor, are we net long or short in a given currency, and how has our exposure profile changed month over month.

columns.asOfDate: The reporting date as of which the FX exposure forecast snapshot was captured, typically month-end.
columns.exposureType: Indicates whether the company holds a net long (asset/receivable) or short (liability/payable) position in the exposure currency.
columns.grossExposure: The total absolute value of the forecasted foreign currency exposure in the base reporting currency, before any hedging offsets are applied.
columns.tenor: The forward time bucket in which the exposure is expected to materialize, such as 0-1 month, 1-3 months, or 3-6 months.
columns.exposureCurrency: The foreign currency in which the exposure is denominated, identifying which currency drives the FX risk for this record.
columns.tradedBy: The trader, desk, or business unit responsible for managing or executing hedges against this specific FX exposure.

FxForward.table_description: The fx_forward table records FX forward contracts used by the treasury department to hedge foreign currency exposure, locking in exchange rates for future settlement dates. Each row represents a single forward contract capturing its full lifecycle from trade execution through settlement. This table supports business questions around hedge coverage, counterparty exposure, settlement scheduling, and trader activity across currency pairs.

columns.code: Unique alphanumeric identifier for the FX forward contract, used to reference and track the instrument across treasury and reporting systems.
columns.status: Current lifecycle status of the forward contract, indicating whether it is active, pending settlement, settled, or cancelled (e.g., SETTLED).
columns.tradeDate: The date on which the FX forward contract was executed and agreed upon between the company and the counterparty.
columns.valueDate: The future date on which the currency exchange will physically settle and funds will be delivered, typically days to months after the trade date.
columns.counterparty: The financial institution or bank on the other side of the forward contract, representing the company's credit and settlement exposure for this trade.
columns.tradedBy: The treasury dealer or trader within the organization who executed and is responsible for this forward contract.
